data.description:
Adds the mutation-append and churn-append subcommands to calibration-report.sh. Each subcommand takes per-PR input (mutation findings JSON, suite churn metrics) and appends a single entry to the appropriate tracking ticket (mutation-history or suite-churn-history). Implements the per-PR append safeguard — either an advisory lock on the tracking ticket or post-append verification — so concurrent fast-follow PR merges produce neither duplicates nor lost entries. This is the critical concurrency surviving scenario from the Red/Blue filter.

## Done Definitions

- calibration-report.sh mutation-append posts a single entry to mutation-history for a given PR's mutation findings ← Satisfies: sc-3
- calibration-report.sh churn-append posts a single entry to suite-churn-history for a given PR's suite churn metrics ← Satisfies: sc-3
- Concurrent invocation of mutation-append (or churn-append) for two distinct PRs produces exactly two entries on the tracking ticket — no duplicates and no lost entries ← Satisfies: sc-6
- Test simulates two concurrent appends (e.g., background subshells racing on the same tracking ticket) and asserts both entries land exactly once ← Satisfies: sc-6
- Running mutation-append (or churn-append) twice for the same PR identifier produces exactly one entry on the tracking ticket — the second invocation detects the existing entry and exits without posting a duplicate ← Satisfies: sc-6

## Considerations

- [Reliability] If the chosen safeguard is an advisory lock, document the lock-release path on script failure (trap on EXIT) so a crashed run does not leave the tracking ticket locked.
- [Reliability] If the chosen safeguard is post-append verification, document the read-after-write window and how the script detects a missed write (e.g., re-read comments and rewrite if the expected entry is absent).

## Escalation Policy

Escalate when blocked
data.title: As CI on a merged PR, I want calibration-report.sh mutation-append and churn-append to record per-PR data onto tracking tickets without duplicates under concurrent merges, so that pre-aggregated data is accurate.
